surfaces.name: Poracode desktop app (Electron; macOS, Windows, Linux)
Poracode CLI, TUI and standalone server (poracode serve)
Web app / PWA served by the host
Built-in app-controls and crossagent MCP servers

claims.answer: Electron desktop app for macOS (DMG, Apple silicon and Intel), Windows (NSIS x64/Arm64) and Linux (AppImage/.deb x64); web/PWA and a CLI/TUI connect to a host; Chrome-family sidebar extension. Native SwiftUI iOS and Compose Android clients exist in the repository, but only a TestFlight upload and an optional Play internal track are documented and no mobile binary is attached to the releases, so public availability is not established.

scope.plan: Open source (Apache-2.0); free, bring your own agents

desktop_os.answer: Installers for macOS (DMG), Windows (NSIS x64/Arm64) and Linux (AppImage, .deb x64); minimum OS versions are not stated in the README.

mobile_apps.answer: Independent native SwiftUI iOS and Compose Android clients (ios/, android/) pair with a host and have a parity ledger; the release docs describe a TestFlight upload and an optional Google Play internal track, and the GitHub releases attach no APK, AAB or IPA, so a public store listing or download is not established.

browser.answer: Web app served by the standalone server and desktop host (`poracode serve --open`), also an installable PWA.

mobile_browser.answer: Mobile web/PWA is a supported client surface ("desktop browser, mobile browser/PWA, native iOS, native Android").

cli.answer: `poracode` CLI opens a TUI, `serve` runs the web app, and `-p "PROMPT" --directory PATH` runs one-shot prompts.

editor_extensions.answer: Chrome/Brave/Edge sidebar extension with chat and browser tools; no IDE (VS Code/JetBrains) extension found (Monaco editor is built into the app).

task_actions.answer: Clients can start, steer, stop and resume threads, resolve approval requests (scope requests:resolve), read terminals and open PR/diff review; viewer scope is read-only.

notifications.answer: OS notifications on desktop and optional push to iOS/Android/web via the host and poracode.com push forwarding.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Host owns sessions; paired desktop, browser, iOS and Android clients project the same threads and reconnect through replay/snapshot recovery.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: editor_extensions; see atomic answers.

claims.answer: Embeds or launches 15+ named harnesses through per-provider adapters (terminal PTY, ACP, SDK or CLI runtimes) plus any ACP-registry or custom ACP agent; crossagent delegation mixes harnesses.

scope.plan: Open source (Apache-2.0); free, bring your own agents

harnesses.answer: Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Grok, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Pi, Qoder, Factory Droid, Antigravity, Cursor, Command Code, Copilot and fx (README); registry also has DeepSeek, Devin and Muse adapters.

model_providers.answer: Models come from each harness; custom model providers can be configured (contracts/modelProviders.ts) and CLI has cliCustomProviders.

custom_adapters.answer: Any agent in the Agent Client Protocol registry or a user-defined acp-generic instance can be installed and run from settings.

session_integration.answer: Terminal-presentation threads run a real PTY of the agent CLI; GUI threads use the provider structured runtime (ACP/SDK/app-server); user picks the runtime where several exist.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Crossagents lets one agent delegate to another provider and experiments run one prompt across several agents in parallel worktrees.

claims.answer: Bring your own: uses each provider CLI/SDK login and API keys directly from the machine; no vendor credits, no Poracode account; local models only through harnesses that support them.

scope.plan: Open source (Apache-2.0); free, bring your own agents

agent_subscriptions.answer: Existing Claude Max, ChatGPT Pro and similar subscriptions are used through each agent login; Live Usage shows session/weekly quota.

api_accounts.answer: README: "Bring your own agent subscriptions & API keys".

vendor_credits.answer: No Poracode credits, paid tier or licence key exist; the FAQ says no paid tier and calls are made directly to providers.

local_models.answer: Local models are possible only when an installed harness (for example OpenCode or custom ACP agents) supports them; Poracode adds no local-model runtime of its own (on-device Whisper is voice input only).

account_switching.answer: Agent profile adapters exist for Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Devin (agentProfiles contracts, profiles.ts), allowing separate logins; breadth per provider not enumerated.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No Poracode account is required; each provider account is the only login (privacy policy: hosts are user-controlled).

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider terms on third-party harness use are not documented in the repository; they are governed by each provider.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: vendor_credits, local_models, account_switching, provider_restrictions; see atomic answers.
claims.unknownReason: Provider terms are external first-party policies, not part of the repository.

scope.plan: Open source (Apache-2.0); free, bring your own agents

first_task_setup.answer: README Getting Started: install Poracode, install the agent CLIs you want, open Poracode, add a project and start.

no_git.answer: Home project scope exists for chats without a repository; whether arbitrary non-Git folders run agents is not stated, and worktree features need Git.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Git operations run locally through the supervisor (status, commit, worktrees); remotes are needed only for PR features.

hosted_git.answer: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Gitea adapters for PRs and reviews.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: README tells the user to install agent CLIs; Linux `libatomic1` and Node requirements are documented for the CLI installer; no consolidated checklist per provider.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: No vendor-managed cloud runtime found in a bounded source search.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: "Remote Machines over SSH" installs Poracode runtime on a host from the user SSH config; standalone server has installer, systemd/launchd units and container image.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: no_git, prerequisite_guidance, managed_cloud_setup; see atomic answers.

cli.answer: `poracode` CLI with TUI, serve, run/-p, admin and host-run commands (src/server/cli*.ts).

api.answer: Authenticated remote-v3 HTTP/WebSocket contract used by web, iOS and Android clients with generated bindings.

sdk.answer: No published client SDK package; packages/ holds agents-usage, codex-protocol and the launcher only.

mcp_server.answer: Built-in app-controls MCP and crossagent MCP expose threads, projects, Git/GitHub, schedules, skills, settings and usage to any agent.

webhooks.answer: No inbound or outbound webhook endpoints found in a bounded search.

operations.answer: MCP/CLI cover create, inspect (read_thread/read_terminal), steer, stop/interrupt, rollback and review of threads.

authentication.answer: Pairing credential, short-lived access tokens with refresh and revocation, scope presets operator/viewer; MCP ingress is local with Host-header gating.

stability.answer: Remote contract is versioned (CLIENT_HOST_HOP_VERSION and remote-v3) but the product is on a nightly 2.0 train; no external API stability promise found.

custom_tools.answer: Custom tools arrive through MCP servers; there is no separate in-app tool-authoring API.

instructions_import.answer: Skills can be browsed from public marketplaces or imported into one shared folder every provider picks up; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are read by harnesses.

sync.answer: No sync with an external tracker found.

supported_edits.answer: Thread metadata (title etc.) editable via update_thread; notes and todos editable in the app.

epics.answer: No epic object found in contracts or MCP tools.

readiness.answer: No readiness model beyond thread status (idle/finished/needs_approval/needs_reply/error).

children.answer: spawn_agent creates child runs and create_thread creates threads.

results.answer: wait_for_agent/wait_for_thread return results; notify_user reports to the human.

evidence.title: Experiment contract
evidence.finding: One prompt run across 2+ candidate threads in separate worktrees from a base commit; judge modes changes/responses; crown a winner then merge or PR.

evidence.title: Experiment judge
evidence.finding: AI judge compares candidate solutions by correctness, bugs, security and returns a winner and per-solution rationale.

evidence.title: Remote access scopes
evidence.finding: Scope list (session read/operate, terminal read/operate, requests:resolve, projects:manage...) with operator and viewer presets; viewer is read-only.

evidence.title: Remote auth
evidence.locator: scopes on grants and sessions, scope_not_granted
evidence.finding: Pairing credential is the scope ceiling; exchanges can only narrow scopes.

evidence.title: Provider registry
evidence.finding: Built-in adapters: Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, Qwen, Pi, Qoder, Factory Droid, Antigravity, Command Code, Copilot, fx, DeepSeek, Devin, Muse, OpenCode, plus generic ACP instances and the ACP registry.

evidence.title: Project notes contract
evidence.finding: Per-project rich-text notes plus a to-do list with done flags; no assignee, priority or dependency fields.

evidence.title: Usage cost history contract
evidence.finding: Token categories (input/output/cache) priced against dated per-model pricing in a currency; cost history by thread.

evidence.title: agents-usage package README
evidence.finding: Collects session/weekly/monthly utilization, resets, plan tier and optional estimated cost for Claude, Codex, Copilot; never logs or persists credentials.

evidence.title: Forge adapters
evidence.finding: Adapters for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea and GitCafe for PRs and reviews.

evidence.title: Supervisor git
evidence.finding: Direct git via execFile: status, diff, stage, revert, commit, branches, fetch, worktree create/remove; worktrees at ~/.poracode/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>.

evidence.title: MCP review tools
evidence.finding: MCP tools for repository reviews, review threads and submissions.

evidence.title: Mobile apps skill
evidence.finding: Independent SwiftUI and Compose clients with a parity ledger; mobile web/PWA also supported.

evidence.title: Native parity ledger
evidence.finding: Tracks per-feature coverage for iOS and Android against the remote contract.

evidence.title: Chrome extension README
evidence.finding: Sidebar chat for Chrome, Brave, Edge connecting to the local app over loopback; no analytics or crash reports from the extension.

evidence.title: CLI package README
evidence.finding: Version-pinned `poracode` launcher with TUI, serve, and `-p` one-shot prompts.

evidence.title: package.json
evidence.finding: Apache-2.0, version 2.0.0-nightly.202611170101, electron-builder targets, bun scripts.

evidence.title: LICENSE
evidence.finding: Apache License 2.0 for the repository.

evidence.title: Host ownership
evidence.finding: One authoritative owner per data root; desktop can attach to a standalone owner over authenticated loopback.

evidence.title: Hero screenshot
evidence.finding: Real Poracode (DEV build) window with two side-by-side agent threads, project sidebar, plan panel and usage rings.

evidence.title: Bounded search: accounts and SSO
evidence.locator: rg saml|oidc|scim|okta|single sign over src/, packages/, native/, tui/src
evidence.finding: No SAML/OIDC/SCIM or user-account system; matches are only provider credential handling for Gemini/Grok/fx.

evidence.title: Bounded search: webhooks and external triggers
evidence.locator: rg webhook over src/, packages/, protocol/
evidence.finding: No inbound webhook or event-trigger endpoint; matches are UI strings/icons only.

evidence.title: Bounded search: managed cloud and container isolation
evidence.finding: No vendor-hosted execution or per-task container/VM isolation; Docker appears only for the server image and server logging.

evidence.title: Bounded search: external trackers and specs
evidence.finding: Linear/Jira/Asana appear only in link-metadata label parsing; no tracker sync and no living-spec feature.

evidence.title: Bounded search: teams and billing
evidence.finding: No organization, seat or billing model in the app; relay comments say billing and hosting sit outside the repo.

evidence.title: Native mobile release
evidence.finding: The Android job builds a signed AAB and publishes to the Google Play internal track only when a service account is configured (otherwise the AAB stays a workflow artifact); the iOS job uploads the IPA to TestFlight. No public store listing or prebuilt mobile download is stated.

evidence.title: Nightly release assets
evidence.locator: release asset list (checked through the GitHub releases API) for v2.0.0-nightly.202611170101 and v1.8.2
evidence.finding: Assets are desktop installers (DMG, zip, NSIS exe, AppImage, deb), server tarballs and update manifests; no APK, AAB or IPA is attached to either release.

evidence.title: Usage service refresh policy
evidence.finding: Usage collection is cached and throttled; the auto-refresh timer is settings-driven with a 5 minute default and a 2 minute floor, and the Muse provider descriptor sets a 15 minute default interval.

evidence.title: Copy ignored files into a new worktree
evidence.finding: When a worktree is created, gitignored files and directories from the main project that match user-configured gitignore-style patterns are copied into it; existing files are not overwritten. This is a copy, not a shared cache.

RUN-04.answer: Worktree setup scripts and port forwarding exist; no shared dependency caches or service snapshots; user diagnoses dependency problems.

dependencies.answer: Worktree scripts (shared/worktreeScriptShell.ts) can run setup commands, and user-configured gitignore-style patterns copy ignored files or directories from the main project into a new worktree; installation is otherwise user-defined.

secrets.answer: Credentials are stored in the OS keychain; there is no per-workspace secret injection, but ignored files such as env files can be copied into a new worktree by pattern.

duplicate_installs.answer: No deduplication across worktrees; ignored dependency directories matched by the copy patterns are copied, not shared.
